===== ORIGINAL PROMPT (initial_prompt.md) =====
Build a visually stunning, fully offline iOS app called "Aura" — a
daily generative "vibe card." Native Apple stack only: SwiftUI +
SwiftData, Core Image / Metal (CIFilter compositions or a custom
Metal shader) for procedural generative art, Swift Charts for the
recap view, StoreKit 2 for local in-app purchases (no backend needed —
App Store handles receipts/entitlements locally). No accounts, no
network, no third-party SDKs — everything on-device, forever. Follow
the ios-app-factory-rules.

CONCEPT: once a day, the user answers 2-3 quick prompts (a mood
picker, one or two tap-to-select word/emoji chips, optionally the
on-device time of day). From that input plus a per-day deterministic
seed, generate a unique abstract generative-art "Aura" card — think
painterly gradient blooms, particle fields, or flow-field line art,
NOT a literal illustration — paired with a short generated caption
built from a curated local phrase bank (never a hallucinated/unsafe
LLM call — this is deterministic, on-device, and instant). The card
must look genuinely beautiful: this is the single most important
requirement in this build. If the generative output looks like
placeholder gradients or a design-101 exercise, the build has failed
its actual goal even if it compiles and passes gates.

CORE FEATURES (favor complete over broad):
1. Daily check-in flow: fast (under 10 seconds), delightful, satisfying
   micro-interactions (haptics, spring animations) on every tap. Once
   completed, locked until the next calendar day (device local time
   zone) — handle timezone travel and DST without allowing two cards
   the "same day" or skipping a day.
2. Generative card engine: a real, documented deterministic algorithm
   mapping (date seed + mood + chips) -> a reproducible but visually
   varied composition (palette, shape field, motion-blur/particle
   density). Same inputs on the same day always render the same card;
   different days must feel meaningfully different from each other,
   not like the same template recolored. This is the technical heart
   of the app — treat it with the same rigor as an algorithm module,
   not incidental UI.
3. Collection & streaks: a scrollable archive/grid of past cards
   (like a photo grid), a streak counter, and a "your Aura over time"
   trend view (mood distribution via Swift Charts).
4. Monthly/seasonal "Wrapped": after each calendar month, generate a
   shareable recap — a short animated sequence or a single composite
   poster of that month's dominant palette/mood story (Spotify-Wrapped
   style). This is a primary viral surface — must render as a
   beautiful, portrait (9:16) export.
5. Share export: every single card AND the monthly Wrapped must export
   as a high-resolution image (and ideally a short looping video/Live
   Photo-style clip of the generative animation) sized correctly for
   Instagram/TikTok Stories (1080x1920), via the native share sheet.
   A small, tasteful, dismissible-only-via-purchase watermark on free
   exports is the monetization hook (see below) — it must never be so
   intrusive it kills the shareability that drives virality.
6. Monetization (StoreKit 2, local only): one non-consumable "Aura+"
   unlock via native IAP removing the export watermark and unlocking
   extra palette themes + the ability to regenerate a card once per
   day if unsatisfied (free tier: no regeneration). Handle purchase,
   restore purchases, and the Simulator's inability to complete real
   StoreKit transactions honestly — use a local StoreKit configuration
   file for Simulator testing and say so explicitly, don't fake a
   purchase succeeding without going through StoreKit's real API.
7. Widget: home-screen widget showing today's card once generated, or
   an inviting "your Aura is waiting" state before check-in.
8. Notifications (local only, opt-in): a gentle daily reminder if the
   user hasn't checked in yet, respecting Focus/Do Not Disturb norms
   and permission denial gracefully.

PRIORITIES, in order: (a) the generative art must be genuinely
beautiful and varied — treat this as a design/craft problem, iterate
on the actual visual output, not just "does it render"; (b) the
deterministic seeding algorithm must be correct and tested (same
inputs -> same card, always); (c) the share-export pipeline must
produce real, correctly-sized, good-looking image/video files, not a
plain screenshot of the UI. Seed a "demo history" toggle with 30+ days
of varied past cards so the archive/Wrapped/trend screens are never
empty on first review. Provide a clear way to run it in the iOS
Simulator via Xcode, and honestly flag anything StoreKit-transaction-
related that cannot be fully verified without a real device/sandbox
account.

--- portfolio_selection (final decision) ---
Both Codex and Claude read this the same way from the start: this is one app, and the phase's real job here was to explicitly confirm that rather than manufacture a split. Codex framed it as a systems-coherence argument (check-in, seed engine, persistence, streaks, and export all share one state model — splitting them would break the daily ritual). Claude framed it as a user-experience argument (the person using this experiences one continuous object — open app, see today's Aura or check in, browse the grid, get Wrapped — and fragmenting that across projects serves internal tidiness, not the user). Both explicitly reject inventing extra apps (no "Aura Lite," no separate widget-app, no companion Watch app, no onboarding-shell app) just because the phase template implies portfolio thinking. No disagreement surfaced — this reads as genuine, immediate convergence on a call that was never really contested.

Claude used the rest of its turn productively: naming the actual failure mode to guard against (a technically-compliant build that reads as "nice SwiftUI gradient exercise" rather than something worth having) and proposing three concrete, checkable success bars for the eventual build/verify phases — first card in under 10 seconds of interaction with no forced tutorial, archive/trend views feeling alive by day 3 of seeded history (not empty-state-as-feature), and a share export that would actually get posted rather than screaming "placeholder." These aren't new decisions in tension with anything — they're operationalizations of what prompt_contract and product_research already locked in (beauty as the hard gate, demo history as non-empty-by-design), stated here because this is the last checkpoint before implementation starts.

## Final Output

Single-app decision: **Aura** is one iOS app project — no portfolio split, no `portfolio-json` manifest, no sibling projects.

- **Selected app:** slug `aura`, category personal wellness + creative ritual + generative art, promise: an offline-first iOS 17+ app turning a short daily mood check-in into a deterministic, cached, high-quality generative card plus a shareable monthly recap, with SwiftData persistence, widget, StoreKit 2 premium unlock, and native share export. Target user: someone who wants a private, on-device daily aesthetic ritual, zero accounts/network. `build = true`.
- **Rejected alternatives:** splitting check-in/gallery/monetization into separate apps; spinning the widget or Wrapped export out as its own deliverable "for cleanliness." Both rejected because the user experiences this as one continuous object, and the underlying systems (seed engine, persistence, streaks) are interdependent enough that a split would fragment the core UX for no real benefit.
- **Scope boundary carried forward:** one app, one bundle identity, one StoreKit non-consumable inside that same app; widget and share extensions stay as extensions of the single target already scoped in `prompt_contract`, not separate projects.
- **Success bar restated for later phases to check against, not just "compiles":** first rendered card reachable in under 10 seconds of active interaction with no forced tutorial; archive/trend views feel alive (not empty-state-pretending-to-be-a-feature) once demo history is seeded; a cold-open share export looks postable, not like a placeholder gradient.

  rejected: Allowing a social/sharing feed of other users' cards; Allowing edits to a locked day's card; Treating a paid regeneration as a second archive entry for the same day
  constraints: Archive/streak logic must treat regeneration as a replace-in-place operation, never an additional record
- [DEC-initial_discussion-007] The exact size of the mood/chip vocabulary and the resulting seed-space dimensionality is explicitly deferred to the generative-algorithm design phase, not decided here.
  rationale: That is an implementation/architecture decision about the seed engine, not a product-promise-level decision this phase should settle by accident.
  rejected: Pre-specifying an exact mood/chip count now
  constraints: Downstream algorithm-design phase owns this decision
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Aura+ (one non-consumable purchase) bundles exactly three functional unlocks: watermark-free exports, an expanded palette library, and one regeneration per day — not cosmetic-only value.
  rationale: A non-consumable unlock still has to keep paying off daily or it reads as a one-time toggle nobody remembers buying; three concrete utility levers make the purchase durable.
  rejected: Cosmetic-only unlock (e.g. just watermark removal); Converting Aura+ to a recurring subscription
  constraints: Purchase remains a single non-consumable IAP per DEC-prompt_contract-002/010
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Regenerated cards must differ from the original in at least two of {palette, shape-field topology, particle/line density} for identical date/mood/chip inputs.
  rationale: A regeneration that reads as a minor recolor breaks the paid feature's emotional promise even if it is technically a distinct render; this is the concrete, testable acceptance bar.
  rejected: Leaving 'visibly different' undefined and trusting subjective judgment at review time
  constraints: Verified by regenerating the same mood/chip pair across multiple days in testing and comparing composition, not just hue
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Target user is narrowed to ~16-34, someone who already runs an adjacent small daily self-care/mood app and checks in during dead-time pockets of their day (coffee, before bed).
  rationale: Design decisions (check-in speed, tone, lack of onboarding) need a specific persona, not a broad demographic; this persona's tolerance for friction is near zero.
  rejected: Broader/generic 'mobile user interested in wellness' framing
  constraints: Check-in speed is treated as a retention feature, not a nice-to-have, per documented mood-app novelty-dropoff risk
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] An on-demand 'so far this month' mini-recap, reusing the Wrapped rendering pipeline at smaller scope, unlocks once a user has 5-7+ real cards banked, rather than waiting for month-end.
  rationale: A genuine new user otherwise gets zero shareable moments for up to 30 days, exactly the window where they decide whether the app earns a permanent home-screen slot — a real gap in the growth mechanism, not a hypothetical.
  rejected: Relying solely on month-end Wrapped as the only viral/recap surface
  constraints: Must reuse the same static composite export pipeline as Wrapped — does not require or imply video/Live Photo export, which remains out of scope
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Build must explicitly audit the SwiftData ModelContainer configuration for cloudKitDatabase: .none (or equivalent) as a concrete guardrail against accidental default CloudKit sync.
  rationale: Several SwiftData project templates default to CloudKit-backed containers; this would silently violate the no-network/no-cloud-dependency requirement already locked in prompt_contract.
  rejected: Trusting that 'no accounts, no network' as a stated principle is sufficient without a concrete build-time check
  constraints: Future v-next cloud sync must be user-opted-in via its own explicit consent screen, never enabled by default container behavior
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Competitive wedge is stated explicitly: Aura is an object-to-own product (deterministic collectible generative artifact), not a data-to-log mood tracker; trend/chart views are a secondary byproduct of collection, not the primary payoff.
  rationale: This is the actual differentiation versus Daylio/How We Feel/Co-Star, who are optimized for insight-over-time with charts as the payoff — naming it concretely should drive UI/tone priority (ceremony over data density) through design and build phases.
  rejected: Framing Aura as a prettier mood-tracking/analytics app
  constraints: Design phases should prioritize the reveal moment and collection feel over dashboard/analytics polish
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Demo-seeded history and freshly-generated cards from equivalent inputs must be visually indistinguishable in rendering quality — distinguishable only by an explicit demo label, never by a quality gap in either direction.
  rationale: If demo data looks better than real output, users sense they're being shown a mockup; if it looks worse, the archive/collection format fails to sell itself during evaluation.
  rejected: Allowing demo cards to use a higher-effort curated rendering path distinct from the real generative engine
  constraints: Acceptance check: 10 demo cards vs. 10 fresh cards from the same mood/chip inputs, side by side, distinguishable only by the demo label
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The daily lock's timezone/DST rule is concretely defined as keying off the last-completed calendar day in the timezone active at the moment of completion, not a naive 'did the wall clock cross midnight' check.
  rationale: This is the exact rule needed to satisfy DEC-prompt_contract-006 without ambiguity, and is the first bug a reviewer finds by changing the Simulator's date/timezone.
  rejected: Any check based on current wall-clock time alone without recording the timezone context at completion
  constraints: Must be verified in build/test by literally changing Simulator date and timezone, not just documented as intent
- [DEC-next_steps_small-001] MVP slice is the full check-in-to-reveal-to-persist loop plus a populated archive grid and one working static share export; Wrapped, widget, notifications, trend charts, and functional StoreKit purchase/restore/regeneration logic are deferred to the next build slice.
  rationale: Proves the core promise end-to-end (deterministic beautiful card, collected, shareable) without the secondary surfaces that are additive polish on top of a working engine.
  rejected: A thinner slice that only proves rendering without persistence/archive/export; Including Wrapped/widget/notifications/StoreKit in the first slice
  constraints: Later build phase must not treat this slice as needing further product debate before implementation
- [DEC-next_steps_small-002] 30+ day labeled demo history stays IN this MVP slice rather than being cut, correcting this round's Codex-fallback proposal which had listed it as cuttable.
  rationale: Already locked upstream in [REDACTED:high_entropy] and DEC-prompt_contract-007 as a v1 must-have; without seeded variety across the seed space, the slice cannot actually validate that adjacent days look meaningfully different, which is the core technical claim of the app.
  rejected: Deferring demo history to a later slice and validating variety with only a handful of manually-generated cards
  constraints: Demo history must remain visibly labeled and never silently blend into real streak/stats, per DEC-prompt_contract-007
- [DEC-next_steps_small-003] One working static 1080x1920 share export with watermark stays IN this MVP slice rather than being cut.
  rationale: Export correctness is explicitly priority (c) in prompt_contract, not a stretch item; validating it only after other features are built risks discovering export/watermark placement problems late.
  rejected: Deferring export entirely to a later slice
  constraints: Full StoreKit purchase logic to remove the watermark is still deferred; only the export pipeline itself and a stubbed/honest paywall affordance are in scope now
- [DEC-next_steps_small-004] The haptic + spring reveal ceremony is a non-negotiable, load-bearing part of the slice and must not be stubbed or skipped under time pressure.
  rationale: Per phase rules ('keep the slice emotionally satisfying, not just technically minimal') and prior phases' framing of Aura as an object-to-receive, not a data-plumbing demo.
  rejected: Shipping an instant, unanimated card reveal to save build time
  constraints: If something must be cut under time pressure, it must not be this
- [DEC-next_steps_small-005] Validation criteria for this slice are: sub-10-second cold-launch-to-revealed-card with no forced tutorial; byte-identical same-day-same-input renders; visually distinct output across 8-10+ combinations (human-eyeballed, not just unit-tested); force-quit non-committing; Simulator date/timezone changes produce no duplicate/skipped day; demo cards visually indistinguishable from real ones except for label; exported image has correct dimensions, no UI chrome, and non-overlapping watermark.
  rationale: Operationalizes the success bars already stated across prior phases into one concrete checklist the build phase can be held to.
  rejected: Leaving validation as general prose without a checkable list
  constraints: These checks must be exercised by literally regenerating/manipulating Simulator state, not just documented as intent
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Caption selection must enforce a no-repeat window (captions not reused within the trailing 30 days for a given mood), with the phrase bank sized to make this achievable.
  rationale: Text repetition is far more noticeable to a user than compositional art variation, and a small bank would surface repeats within weeks of daily use, undermining the 'never feels templated' promise.
  rejected: Leaving caption bank sizing/repetition unaddressed and discovering collisions only through real usage
  constraints: Deterministic selection must still be reproducible per day, drawing only from the eligible (non-recently-used) subset
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The regeneration credit and the daily lock must be tracked from one shared canonical 'last completed calendar day' state, not two independent date checks.
  rationale: If regeneration uses its own naive date comparison, rolling the device clock back and forward grants unlimited free regenerations, breaking the one-per-day paid feature's premise even though the daily-lock backward-clock rule (DEC-prompt_contract-006) was already satisfied.
  rejected: Tracking regeneration eligibility with a separate 'used today: bool' reset on its own date comparison
  constraints: Build phase must implement both the daily lock and regeneration credit against the same state source
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The app must explicitly trigger a WidgetKit timeline reload as part of the check-in completion path, not rely on WidgetKit picking up the new card unassisted.
  rationale: WidgetKit doesn't know a new card exists unless told; a missed or delayed reload leaves the widget showing 'your Aura is waiting' after the user already checked in, directly undermining the widget's role as the durable retention channel identified in product_research.
  rejected: Assuming WidgetKit's normal timeline refresh cadence is sufficient
  constraints: Must be a testable, explicit step in the check-in completion code path
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Pending local daily-reminder notifications must be cancelled/rescheduled immediately on successful check-in; notification permission is requested contextually (after first completed check-in or via Settings), never at first launch; a denied permission gets a deep link back to Settings.app.
  rationale: An uncancelled reminder for an already-completed check-in erodes trust in a ritual app; requesting permission at first launch tanks opt-in and violates HIG guidance; a denied permission needs a real path back in rather than a dead end.
  rejected: Requesting notification permission at first app launch; Leaving scheduled notifications unmanaged after check-in completes
  constraints: Cancellation must be part of the check-in completion transaction, not a best-effort background step
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Demo history occupies a fixed historical date range strictly before install/first real check-in (collision with real check-in dates is structurally impossible), and disabling demo mode shows an explicit confirmation that the streak will reset to real check-ins only.
  rationale: Runtime conflict resolution between demo and real days on the same date is a bug surface that shouldn't exist; a silent streak-number drop when toggling demo mode off reads as an app bug rather than expected behavior.
  rejected: Allowing demo history to keep generating forward while enabled, requiring runtime date-collision handling; Silently changing the displayed streak count when demo mode is toggled off
  constraints: Demo date range must be computed once, anchored before real usage begins
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] StoreKit entitlement state must be kept current via a live Transaction.updates listener, not only a one-time check at launch; this is documented as its own honest verification gap separate from Simulator's inability to complete real transactions.
  rationale: Without a live listener, a refund or a restore on another path won't reflect in the app until the next cold launch, which is invisible to Simulator-only testing and could let a refunded user keep premium features for a session.
  rejected: Checking Transaction.currentEntitlements only once at app launch
  constraints: Honesty disclaimer for StoreKit verification must name this gap distinctly from DEC-prompt_contract-008's transaction-completion caveat
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] A SwiftData store load failure (corruption, disk full, future migration failure) must be detected and surfaced as an explicit error state, never silently treated as a fresh empty store.
  rationale: The entire product value is the accumulated card collection; silently starting a user over with zero cards on a load failure is a direct betrayal of the 'archive worth protecting' promise.
  rejected: Letting a failed store load fall through to an empty-state UI indistinguishable from a genuine fresh install
  constraints: Error state must be distinguishable from the genuine empty-state (new user) UI
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Card accessibility descriptions are generated from mood/chip/caption metadata (e.g. 'a warm, calm morning aura'), not attempted visual/pixel description; mood/chip pickers must be distinguishable by non-color means (shape/icon/label) for color-blind users.
  rationale: VoiceOver cannot meaningfully describe an abstract generative composition, and an entirely palette-organized picker UI is unusable for color-blind users without a non-color differentiator.
  rejected: Omitting meaningful accessibility descriptions for generative cards; Relying on color alone to distinguish mood/chip options
  constraints: Applies to card detail views, archive grid, and widget
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Exported images must not leak EXIF/device metadata, and the watermark asset must be fully bundled in the app, never fetched remotely.
  rationale: A remotely-fetched watermark asset would be a network call at the exact moment of sharing, violating the no-network requirement; metadata leakage is a privacy concern for a supposedly private, on-device app.
  rejected: Fetching or updating the watermark asset remotely for easier iteration
  constraints: Applies to both per-card export and Wrapped export
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The 8-10+ combination visual-review checkpoint (DEC-prompt_contract-003) is explicitly blocked on the mood/chip vocabulary being fixed by the algorithm-design phase; that phase owns unblocking it, not just picking a vocabulary size in isolation.
  rationale: There is no defined sample universe for the visual-review checkpoint until the vocabulary size is fixed, so the dependency needs to be named explicitly rather than assumed to resolve itself.
  rejected: Treating vocabulary-size deferral (DEC-initial_discussion-007) as unrelated to the visual-review checkpoint's readiness
  constraints: Algorithm-design phase must treat 'unblocks visual-review checkpoint' as part of its deliverable, not a side effect
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] Entitlement changes (e.g. purchasing Aura+ mid-day) must never retroactively mutate an already-persisted card's render; only cards generated after the purchase, plus a spent regeneration credit, may reflect the new entitlement.
  rationale: Preserves the render-once-persist-forever architecture ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) and the core determinism guarantee; computing the active palette set live from current entitlement would let the same (date+mood+chips) seed produce different output depending purely on purchase timing.
  rejected: Computing the active palette/entitlement set live at render or view time instead of snapshotting it
  constraints: Entitlement state used for rendering must be snapshotted and stored with the card record at generation time, same as other seed inputs
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The international date-line / transoceanic travel edge case is resolved explicitly as 'local calendar day wins,' accepting that this can legitimately produce two check-ins within under 24 real-world hours (eastward travel) or an apparent one-day streak gap (westward travel) for a traveler who did nothing wrong.
  rationale: This is a materially different case from the already-solved DST/backward-clock cheating scenario; avoids over-engineering a vanishingly rare edge case with elapsed-real-time tracking, which would also risk destabilizing the already-correct simpler rule.
  rejected: Tracking elapsed real-world hours between check-ins to prevent double-checkin or apparent gaps from transoceanic travel
  constraints: This is a named, accepted limitation, not a bug — must not motivate later ad hoc complexity that risks breaking the DST/backward-clock rule
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The WidgetKit timeline reload trigger ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) must fire on both check-in completion and successful regeneration, as two distinct call sites.
  rationale: A regenerated card is a second point where the persisted render changes; without its own explicit reload trigger, the widget shows a stale pre-regeneration card exactly like the original check-in-completion bug it was meant to fix.
  rejected: Assuming the check-in-completion reload trigger also covers regeneration
  constraints: Must be implemented and tested as two separate trigger points in code, not one shared assumption
- [[REDACTED:high_entropy]] The restore-purchases success confirmation must explicitly state that card history/streak stays device-local and is not restored or backed up, distinct from the entitlement itself which is restored.
  rationale: Combines two already-locked boundaries (no cross-device/reinstall continuity, and an honest restore-purchases success state) that collide into a real support/perception gap: a reinstall+restore correctly returns Aura+ but leaves an empty archive, which reads as data loss next to a bare 'restored!' banner.
  rejected: A generic 'purchase restored' confirmation with no mention of local-only history
  constraints: Applies specifically to the restore-purchases success path, distinct from DEC-prompt_contract-008's honest 'nothing to restore' state
- [DEC-app_features-001] Full feature set is prioritized must/should/could/won't rather than treating the prompt's eight feature bullets as eight equal must-haves.
  rationale: Some prompt features (widget, notifications, Wrapped, trend charts) are explicitly secondary/dependent per upstream product_research and per_app_product_brief decisions; restating all eight as equal musts would misrepresent already-settled prioritization.
  rejected: Treating every one of the prompt's eight numbered features as an equal must-have
  constraints: requirements-json core:true set maps to must-have; core:false maps to should/could/guardrail
- [DEC-app_features-002] Full StoreKit 2 wiring (purchase, restore, live entitlement listener, regeneration-entitlement rules) stays a must-have for this full build, but is explicitly flagged as the single riskiest must-have; if scope must be trimmed under time pressure, trim within StoreKit's three unlocks (e.g. ship watermark removal + one regeneration correctly, treat expanded palette themes as could) rather than rushing the core engine or export pipeline.
  rationale: StoreKit is explicitly core to the prompt and this phase scopes the full build (not another MVP slice), but it is also the item where 'what's implemented' and 'what Simulator can prove' diverge most, and where the four already-locked entitlement rules are easiest to silently violate under time pressure.
  rejected: Demoting StoreKit to should/could to reduce risk; Treating StoreKit as equally low-risk as the rest of the must-have list
  constraints: If cut, cut inside StoreKit's own three unlocks, never by rushing the generative engine or export pipeline
- [DEC-app_features-003] Widget and local notifications are scored as should-have, not must-have, for this build.
  rationale: Both are real retention value but are second surfaces layered on an already-working render pipeline, and were already explicitly deferred once in next_steps_small for the same reason; a locked IA/behavior decision (e.g. widget deep-link, dual reload triggers) governs how they're built if built, but doesn't promote their priority.
  rejected: Treating widget/notifications as must-haves because they were both in the original prompt's numbered feature list
  constraints: If built, must still follow the already-locked widget-deep-link and dual-reload-trigger rules from initial_discussion and detailed_discussion
- [DEC-app_features-004] Monthly Wrapped, the on-demand mini-recap, and the mood-distribution trend view are scored as should-have, not must-have.
  rationale: Consistent with product_research calling Wrapped 'secondary/dependent' and per_app_product_brief framing trend/chart views as a byproduct of collection rather than the payoff.
  rejected: Promoting Wrapped to must-have given the prompt calls it a primary viral surface
  constraints: Trend view stays nested inside Archive per DEC-initial_discussion-002 if built; mini-recap reuses the Wrapped static pipeline per [REDACTED:high_entropy] if built
- [DEC-app_features-005] Could-list is defined as: additional palette themes beyond the Aura+ baseline, a richer caption bank beyond the 30-day no-repeat minimum, additional widget size variants, onboarding polish beyond the zero-tutorial requirement, and accessibility refinements beyond the metadata-description baseline.
  rationale: None of these block the core product promise if cut; they are enhancements on top of already-must-have baselines.
  rejected: Leaving the could-list undefined and deciding ad hoc during build
  constraints: Could-items must not be built at the expense of any must-have
- [DEC-app_features-006] Won't-build list is restated explicitly as this phase's contract: no social/feed layer, no editing/undoing a locked day, no second archive record for regeneration, no cross-device/iCloud sync or reinstall continuity, no video/Live Photo export, no analytics/crash SDKs, no third-party dependencies.
  rationale: These were already decided in principle across earlier phases; restating them here makes them part of this phase's explicit machine-readable contract rather than only implied by earlier prose.
  rejected: Leaving these boundaries implicit rather than restated in this phase's own output
  constraints: Later build/verify phases check the built app against this list as explicit non-goals, not just must-haves
- [DEC-app_features-007] Every acceptance criterion in the requirements-json contract must be phrased as a concrete, reviewer-executable action (e.g. 'change the Simulator's date/timezone and confirm no duplicate/skipped day') rather than a vague adjective (e.g. 'handles timezone correctly').
  rationale: Vague acceptance criteria are exactly how a technically-compliant, visually-mediocre build passes the gate — the failure mode portfolio_selection already named as the one to guard against.
  rejected: Allowing prose-level acceptance criteria without concrete reviewer actions
  constraints: Later build/verify phases must be graded against the concrete phrasing in requirements-json, not a looser restatement
- [DEC-design_discussion-001] App design language is named 'Dusk Gallery': dark-first, low-contrast chrome, translucent frosted surfaces letting each card's palette bleed into surrounding UI, generous negative space, motion on slow physical springs.
  rationale: The persona checks in half-asleep or pre-bed; the chrome must recede so the generative card reads as the one considered object on screen, like a piece in an underlit gallery room, distinct from what a productivity or logging app would want.
  rejected: Generic 'clean and modern' styling with no named rationale
  constraints: Applies to all screens: Today, Archive, Wrapped, Settings
- [DEC-design_discussion-002] Emotional target is locked: the user should feel like something was quietly made for them today, worth a few seconds of attention — anticipation resolving into specific delight, never gamified urgency or clinical logging.
  rationale: Gives later phases a concrete bar for tone in copy, animation pacing, and interaction design.
- [DEC-design_discussion-003] Signature interaction is the live bloom reveal: after the final chip tap, the actual Core Image/Metal generative pipeline renders on-screen over ~1.5-2s with three distinct haptic beats (light/medium/heavy-confirm), caption fading in half a beat after the art settles.
  rationale: The app's premise ('made for you today') depends on the reveal visibly being the real engine constructing output live, not a canned animation over a pre-rendered static image.
  rejected: Instant pop-in of the finished card; A generic push/fade transition to a static image; Pre-rendering the animation separately from the actual generative output
  constraints: Reveal must invoke the real rendering pipeline, not a decorative animation layered on top of an already-finished image
- [DEC-design_discussion-004] The stock/default UI approach (system List rows for archive, segmented Picker for mood, generic share-sheet screenshot, UIKit alert for purchase, default large-title NavigationStack chrome) is explicitly rejected in favor of: a custom palette-tinted grid for archive, a cluster of tactile icon+label shapes for mood/chip selection, the live bloom reveal, and a minimal custom top bar with no default large-title box.
  rationale: Each default pattern actively undermines the collection/ritual framing (list reads as data, segmented control reads as settings, large-title box creates a visible seam in dark mode) or fails accessibility (color-only mood/chip differentiation excludes colorblind users).
  rejected: Using default SwiftUI List/Picker/NavigationStack chrome for speed of implementation
  constraints: Build phase must implement custom grid, custom picker shapes, and custom top bar rather than stock components
- [DEC-design_discussion-005] Today screen has six distinct states: cold-launch skeleton, not-yet-checked-in (dim unlit aura silhouette), check-in steps (mood then chip, time-of-day resolved silently), bloom reveal, settled revealed state (with regeneration visibly gated, not hidden, for free users), and a store-load-failure error state visually and textually distinct from the genuine new-user empty state.
  rationale: Conflating a store-load failure with a genuine empty state would silently read as data loss, the exact failure mode already warned against upstream; showing free users a visibly-gated (not hidden) regenerate affordance surfaces the paid feature as a real upsell rather than an invisible one.
  rejected: Treating store-load failure and new-user-empty as the same UI state; Hiding the regenerate affordance entirely for free-tier users
  constraints: Widget tap must deep-link to whichever of these six states is currently true, not just foreground the app to a default screen
- [DEC-design_discussion-006] Archive grid cells carry the demo-history badge directly on the cell itself, in addition to a dismissible top banner while demo mode is active; a genuine empty state is a designed icon+line+CTA, never bare 'no cards yet' text.
  rationale: Banners get scrolled past; the grid must remain self-explanatory about demo-vs-real status even after a user forgets the banner exists, per the already-locked demo-labeling requirement.
  rejected: Relying solely on a top banner to indicate demo mode is active
  constraints: Applies per-cell in the archive grid, not just at the screen level
- [DEC-design_discussion-007] Wrapped shows an explicit 'not yet unlocked, check in a few more days' state before the first month boundary or mini-recap threshold is reached, rather than appearing empty or broken.
  rationale: Wrapped is one of four named nav destinations; a dormant-looking tab reads as a bug rather than a feature that hasn't unlocked yet.
  rejected: Leaving the Wrapped tab in a generic empty state indistinguishable from a broken screen
  constraints: Applies until either the first calendar month boundary or the 5-7+ card mini-recap threshold is met
- [DEC-design_discussion-008] Caption text over generative art requires a defined legibility treatment (scrim, frosted text plate, or adaptive text color sampled from the underlying art), and the bloom reveal requires an explicit Reduce Motion fallback (a gentler crossfade preserving the same haptic beats), decided now rather than left to build-time discovery.
  rationale: Caption legibility against an arbitrary busy composition and Reduce Motion support for the app's single signature moment are both concrete failure risks that a generic 'add accessibility later' approach would miss.
  rejected: Leaving caption contrast unaddressed until a real collision is found in testing; Simply disabling the bloom animation for Reduce Motion with no alternate reveal
  constraints: Reduce Motion fallback must preserve the same haptic beats as the full bloom, only removing the physical motion
- [DEC-design_handoff-001] A single @MainActor @Observable AuraStore, injected via environment, is the sole owner of the canonical last-completed-calendar-day value, entitlement snapshot, and demo-mode state; no view or screen independently queries SwiftData to compute its own notion of 'today' or entitlement.
  rationale: The daily-lock/regeneration-credit shared-day-state rule ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) and entitlement-snapshotting rule ([REDACTED:high_entropy]) are only actually shared if there is one source of truth in code; scattered per-view @Query-based date/entitlement checks are exactly how those two rules would silently drift apart under a clock change.
  rejected: Per-screen @Query-based computation of day-state and entitlement
  constraints: Build phase must implement one AuraStore instance injected via environment, not per-screen state duplication
- [DEC-design_handoff-002] Navigation is a TabView with a fully custom tab bar (not just custom NavigationStack chrome) — stock translucent tab bar material is explicitly rejected because it double-blurs against Dusk Gallery's own frosted surfaces; each tab owns its own NavigationStack driven by a typed route enum (TodayRoute, ArchiveRoute, WrappedRoute), with a single PendingDeepLink value on the store consumed once via .onChange to resolve widget taps into the correct tab + path + Today sub-state.
  rationale: The widget-tap-must-land-on-exact-current-state requirement (DEC-initial_discussion-003, DEC-design_discussion-005) has no concrete implementation path without a programmatic deep-link mechanism external to the view hierarchy; raw NavigationLink(destination:) cannot be pushed into from outside the tree.
  rejected: Stock translucent tab bar material; Raw NavigationLink(destination:) navigation without a typed route/deep-link mechanism
  constraints: Build phase must implement PendingDeepLink + typed route enums, not ad hoc navigation state
- [DEC-design_handoff-003] The widget extension requires an App Group shared container holding cached rendered PNGs plus card/palette metadata; the widget reads only this shared cache and never touches the main app's ModelContext directly.
  rationale: This is invisible until the widget target is actually wired up and easy to skip under time pressure since the main app functions fine without it; without it, the widget cannot read the cached-render architecture already mandated by [REDACTED:high_entropy].
  rejected: Widget reading the app's default sandboxed Documents directory or ModelContext directly
  constraints: Must be an explicit line item (app group identifier, shared container URL) in the build handoff
- [DEC-design_handoff-004] The bloom reveal's 'real engine, not a decorative animation' requirement is concretely defined as: 4 genuine cached intermediate composites (seed-point/palette wash, shape-field placement, particle/line density pass, final color grade) generated once at render time from the actual filter/shader chain, cross-dissolved along the spring timeline with the three haptic beats aligned to the 1→2, 2→3, and 3→4(settle) transitions.
  rationale: Literally re-stepping the CIFilter/Metal composite graph every display frame in sync with a spring curve would jank on older supported devices; without a concrete definition, 'real engine' either becomes a performance trap or gets quietly faked as a crossfade over one pre-rendered static image, which would be invisible in review.
  rejected: Re-running the full filter/shader chain live on every display frame; A crossfade/decorative animation layered over a single pre-rendered final image

# Common iOS & SwiftUI Pitfalls: Symptoms and Fixes

Reference for building iPhone apps on **iOS 17+ / Swift 5.9+** (validated against Xcode 26 / Swift 6). Each entry is **symptom → fix** with compilable, idiomatic code. First-party frameworks only; zero third-party dependencies.

## 0. Fast rules (read first)

- Prefer `@Observable` (Observation framework, iOS 17+) over `ObservableObject`/`@Published` for new view models.
- All UI mutation happens on the main actor. Never call SwiftUI/UIKit off-main.
- `Task {}` inherits the enclosing actor and priority; `Task.detached {}` inherits neither. Know which you want.
- A view's `body` is a pure function of its inputs. It can run many times per second — keep it cheap and side-effect-free.
- Every `ForEach` element needs a **stable** identity. Never key on array index for mutable data.
- `@State` is for view-local, view-owned, transient state — nothing else.
- When generating a project headlessly, the `.pbxproj`/target membership, bundle id, and signing config matter as much as the Swift code. A perfect source file that isn't in the target does not compile.

---

## 1. Main-thread / UI updates

### 1.1 Mutating UI state from a background thread

**Symptom:** Purple runtime warning "Publishing changes from background threads is not allowed"; UI updates late, flickers, or crashes; `_dispatch_assert_queue_fail`.

**Cause:** State that drives the UI is written from a background queue (e.g. a `URLSession` completion handler, a `DispatchQueue.global` block, a C callback).

**Fix — hop to the main actor before touching UI state:**

```swift
// WRONG: completion handler runs on a background thread
URLSession.shared.dataTask(with: url) { data, _, _ in
    self.items = decode(data)   // ❌ background-thread UI mutation
}.resume()

// RIGHT: async/await keeps you on the caller's actor
@MainActor
func load() async throws {
    let (data, _) = try await URLSession.shared.data(from: url)
    items = try JSONDecoder().decode([Item].self, from: data) // ✅ on main
}
```

If you're stuck with a callback API, bridge explicitly:

```swift
someLegacyAPI { result in
    Task { @MainActor in
        self.items = result   // ✅ explicit hop to main
    }
}
```

- Do **not** sprinkle `DispatchQueue.main.async` everywhere as a superstition. Model the actor boundary once (usually `@MainActor` on the view model) and let the compiler enforce it.
- `@Observable` classes are **not** implicitly main-actor. Mark the type `@MainActor` if it owns UI state.

### 1.2 Blocking the main thread with sync work

## 2. async/await, Task, and @MainActor

### 2.1 `Task {}` vs `Task.detached {}`

**Symptom:** Either an unexpected main-thread hop, or a data-race warning, depending on which you picked by accident.

**Rule:**
- `Task {}` **inherits** the current actor, priority, and task-local values. Inside a `@MainActor` type, its body runs on the main actor.
- `Task.detached {}` inherits **nothing** — no actor, no priority, no task-locals. Use it only for genuinely independent background work (and reach for it rarely; a `nonisolated` async function is usually the cleaner way to get off-main).

```swift
@MainActor
final class FeedModel {
    var state: LoadState = .idle
    let api: API

    init(api: API) { self.api = api }

    func refresh() {
        Task {                    // ✅ runs on MainActor; safe to touch state
            state = .loading
            let feed = (try? await api.fetch()) ?? []
            state = .loaded(feed)
        }
    }
}
```

- Prefer structured concurrency (`async let`, `TaskGroup`) over spawning unstructured `Task {}` when results must be awaited.

### 2.2 Fire-and-forget tasks that outlive the view

**Symptom:** "Modifying state during view update" logs; work continues after the view disappears; wasted network calls; crashes touching a deallocated model.

**Fix — bind the task lifetime to the view with `.task`:**

```swift
struct FeedView: View {
    @State private var model = FeedModel(api: .live)

    var body: some View {
        List(model.items) { ItemRow(item: $0) }
            .task { await model.load() }   // ✅ auto-cancelled on disappear
    }
}
```

- `.task(id:)` re-runs when `id` changes and cancels the previous run — the correct way to react to a changing parameter (e.g. a selected user id).

### 2.3 Ignoring cancellation

**Symptom:** A search-as-you-type view fires a request per keystroke and races; stale results overwrite fresh ones.

**Fix — debounce inside `.task(id:)`, which cancels the previous run on each new keystroke:**

```swift
.task(id: query) {
    do {
        try await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(300)) // debounce; throws on cancel
        results = try await search(query)
    } catch {
        // CancellationError from a superseded keystroke, or a search failure.
        // Either way, don't overwrite fresh results with stale/empty data.
    }
}
```
